label: Diagnostics for bug reports
changes: **The engine reports on itself for a bug report.** Home's new Control panel › Infrastructure › Diagnostics page asks it for its version and machine, the ffmpeg it runs, what the GPU check found, its conversion settings, its libraries' counts and states, and the warnings and errors in its log. Home hides names, folders and addresses unless the admin asks to include them, and nothing leaves home unless the admin copies the report out. Needs isputnik.home 4.89.0 to be seen.

**The GPU's recent failures are kept with ffmpeg's own words.** The last ten, each with when it happened and whether it counted towards setting the GPU aside (a film without HDR mastering data doesn't). Before, only the count was kept, so a report of "the GPU isn't used" came with nothing to go on.

label: Posters past a sleeping disk
changes: **Scrolling past posters no longer waits on a sleeping disk.** A poster or backdrop kept beside a film was looked up in a way that held the whole engine, so a page of posters from a disk that had spun down stopped everyone, people watching something else included, until it was up again. It is now looked up without holding anything, as the films themselves have been since 0.37.0.
**A poster taken away from beside its film is simply not there.** One removed after the engine had found it answered with an error; it now answers that there is no such picture.

label: Answers through every scan
changes: **The engine keeps answering while it scans.** A scan read the whole library in one go and nothing else got a turn until it finished: on a big library on a NAS share that was minutes with no health check, no page and no video, and the container showed as unhealthy. The disk is now read a little at a time between other work, and the catalog written from it in one short step. A library a stop left marked as queued or scanning is set back on start.

**No more minutes of silence after a scan.** The pass that looks for posters and TMDB details went over every title after every scan, rewrote each one even when nothing had changed, and worked its cast and crew out again from scratch. It now writes only what changed, works out the cast only of titles that got new people, lists each folder once, and lets other work in between titles. Scanning the cast of the whole catalog, which the scan did too, is now done only for titles added, removed or with another cast in their .nfo. On a test library of 2000 films the engine stopped answering for about 10 seconds per scan; now for well under one.

**A sleeping disk no longer stops everyone.** Finding a film's file, the subtitles beside it and its .edl waited on the disk in a way that held the whole engine: when the disk holding one film had spun down, people watching something else waited for it too. Those lookups now wait on their own. The folder picker in Add library, and finding intros and credits after a scan, do the same.

**Intros and credits are looked for when nobody is watching.** That work went on while someone watched a converted film, taking cores and disk from them. It now waits between seasons and films while someone is watching, as copies for download already did. Find again from home still runs at once.

**Switching quality mid-film no longer restarts the conversion over and over.** A segment of the old quality still on its way stopped the new one's conversion to start its own, and the two took turns, about 20 times in two seconds. The quality whose playlist the player asked for last is now the one being played, and a late request for another is turned away without being asked again.

**Films played before 0.31.0 no longer read the whole file again.** Probing a film again for what 0.31.0 added threw away where its keyframes are, though the file had not changed, so each such film's next play had to read it all through. They are now kept while the file stays the same.

**HDR films can be tone-mapped on an Intel GPU.** The start-up check always said the GPU could not tone-map, because its test picture carried none of the mastering details an HDR10 film has and the GPU refuses a picture without them. The test picture has them now. HLG films, which usually carry none, are tone-mapped on the CPU, and a film the GPU refuses for want of them goes to the CPU without counting against the GPU.

**Backups are taken a little at a time.** The catalog was copied for a backup in one piece in memory; it is now copied with SQLite's own backup between other work and streamed to home, and the copy a restore keeps for undoing it is made the same way.

label: Released for real
changes: **0.35.0 and 0.36.0 reach the image at last.** Neither was published: the tests that run before the image is built failed, because the ffmpeg they used (a separate build, not the one the image ships) crashed whenever it put an MPEG-TS video into an MP4, which is how a copy for download is finished. The tests now use the same kind of ffmpeg as the image. This release carries everything in 0.35.0 (converting in memory unless /transcode is a disk, one shared conversion, films kept once converted, Keep ready) and 0.36.0 (big films start sooner).
**A copy for download is put together from one stream.** Its kept pieces are now handed to ffmpeg one after another rather than through a list file: simpler, and nothing left behind if it stops.

label: Big films start sooner
changes: **The first play of a big MKV no longer waits for the whole file to be read.** A film whose picture is sent as it is can only be cut where its keyframes are, and the engine used to find them by reading every byte of the file. On a 30 GB Blu-ray rip on an array disk that took several minutes (longer than the player waited), so the film sat on "Getting it ready…" or failed to start the first time. The keyframes now come from the file's own index, checking each one the way ffmpeg does, since MakeMKV and mkvmerge mark more frames than ffmpeg can cut on: seconds instead of minutes. A file whose index won't do is read as before.

**Keyframes are read ahead.** After each scan and when the engine starts, it reads the keyframes of the titles that will need them, one file at a time and never starting a new one while someone is watching, so even a file that has to be read whole is ready before anyone presses Play.

label: Memory first, one cache, kept ready
changes: **Converted video stays out of the container.** The engine now checks whether `/transcode` is a disk mapped into the container. If it isn't (the Unraid template's Transcode path left empty), video is converted in memory only and no copies for download are prepared there, so nothing fills `docker.img`. With a disk, the admin picks memory only, memory then the disk (the default), or the disk only, and one memory limit is shared by everyone watching (a tenth of the server's memory, at most 1 GB, to start with). isputnik.home 4.88 shows the disk and its free space on Settings › Video › Converting video. Older homes keep working with their memory-per-viewer setting.

**One conversion per version, shared.** Two people watching the same film at the same quality and sound track now share one conversion instead of making it twice, and joining a film someone is already watching takes no place from the household's limit.

**Films kept once converted all the way through.** With a disk, a film whose picture had to be re-encoded is kept once someone has watched it to the end, so it plays next time with nothing converted, also after a restart. A film left at 70% or more is finished off in the background so it is kept too. Kept films and copies for download share one limit (Room for kept video, 50 GB to start with); the ones used longest ago go first.

**Copies for download are made through the same cache.** A copy whose picture is re-encoded is made as the version a viewer would get, a stretch at a time and resumable, then put together into the MP4 in seconds. Copies asked for are carried on after a restart.

**Keep ready.** An admin can keep a film, a show or one season ready at 1080p, 720p or 480p (`/admin/keep-ready`): converted ahead of time in the background and never removed to make room. A show's new episodes follow unless asked not to.

**When downloads are prepared.** The queue runs right away, only when the server is idle, or only between two times at night, with a number of jobs at once and a limit on how many downloads one member may have waiting (`/admin/jobs`). Copies going to someone away from home can be held to a download speed so streaming keeps its share of the upload link.

label: Off the row, and new again
changes: **Take something off Continue watching.** `DELETE /video/api/continue/:id` takes a show (asked by any of its episodes) or a film (every part of it) off the row for the person asking, so isputnik.home 4.86 can offer **Remove from Continue watching** on each card. Nothing is forgotten: the place in it stays, and playing it again, or marking it watched or unwatched, brings it back. Before, a film abandoned halfway or a show nobody meant to go on with stayed on the row for good.
**Every film and show card says when it came** (`addedAt`), so home can keep **Recently added** to the last weeks instead of calling a years-old title new just because nothing came after it.

**A new season makes a show new again.** A show is now dated by the later of when it was first found and when the scan last found an episode it didn't have, so it moves back to the top of Recently added. A file renamed or moved to another folder, with the same season and episode number, doesn't count. Episodes found before this version don't count either: only those the scan finds from now on.

label: Copies prepared for download
changes: **A download optimized for a phone or tablet is now prepared here, on a queue.** isputnik.home 4.82 asks for a smaller copy of a film or episode (480p, 720p or 1080p); the engine makes it as one MP4 and the device fetches the finished file at full speed. Before, the film was converted while the phone waited on the connection, which was slow and loaded the server for as long as the download took.

**Kind to the server.** One copy is made at a time, on the GPU where there is one; without one, at low priority and with half the CPU's cores. A copy being made stands still while anyone is watching converted video, and carries on after.

**Kept for the next person.** A copy made once serves everyone who may see that title. Together they stay under a size set in home's Settings → Video → **Copies for download** (20 GB to start with); past it, the ones used longest ago go. A copy of a file that has changed since is made again.

**Where they are kept:** in a `copies` folder inside `/transcode` when that is mapped, otherwise beside the catalog. Map `/transcode` to a disk with room for them. The conversion folder is still emptied on start, but no longer the copies in it.
A 1080p copy is held to about 2.5 GB for a two-hour film, lower than a 1080p stream; 720p is about 1.4 GB and 480p about 0.7 GB.

label: What you have watched
changes: **Every card says where you are in it.** The lists isputnik.home draws its posters from now carry, for the person asking, a film's place (a film in several files counting as one) and a show's count of episodes seen, so home 4.81 can draw a bar on a film left part-way, a check on a finished one and "8 unwatched" on a show, without a request per poster.

**A list narrows by it.** `/titles?watch=` takes unwatched, progress and watched, any of them: home's new Watched filter. A show counts as watched only once every episode is, so a new episode brings it back.

**A whole show, a season or a film is marked in one call.** `PUT /video/api/watched/:kind/:id` marks every episode of a show, or of one season, or every part of a film, watched or never seen, for the person asking. Marked watched, what follows them is next: seasons 1 to 3 make season 4's first episode next up. Marked unwatched, their history goes and nothing is left to resume. Before, only one episode or film could be marked at a time.
Each person's marks, and each viewing profile's, stay their own, as progress always was.

label: On Docker Hub, and ready for Unraid Community Applications
changes: **The image is on Docker Hub too, as isputnikdotnet/isputnik.video.** Every release tag publishes the same image to ghcr.io and to Docker Hub, as isputnik.home's does, and the Docker Hub page shows this README under a description that says what the container is: an add-on for isputnik.home. Every public description now says so: the GitHub repository, the image, the Unraid template and its profile.

**Ready for Unraid Community Applications as isputnik-video.** The template now publishes port 4300 on the ordinary bridge network, so isputnik.home reaches the engine at the server's own address with nothing to create first; a shared Docker network or br0 with a fixed IP work as before. It sends the administrator to isputnik.home's Control panel → Settings → Apps for the pairing, where the secret is generated first and pasted into Gateway Secret, and it carries this change log, regenerated by `npm run changelog` on every release.

label: Quality for viewers away from home
changes: **Quality rungs.** The player's Quality menu in isputnik.home 4.78 asks this engine for Original, 1080p, 720p or 480p, made while the film plays; a film already smaller than the rung is sent as it is. Someone watching from outside the home network is held under the cap set in Settings → Video (up to 720p to start with), read from the gateway's network header, because a Blu-ray rip sent as it is needs more upload than a home link has.

label: Profiles keep their own history
changes: **Viewing profiles keep their own history.** Continue watching, watched marks and My list belong to the profile isputnik.home 4.76 forwards, the same on every TV and browser, so the cartoons stay out of the grown-ups' Continue watching.

label: Without Stremio
changes: **The Stremio add-on's routes are gone**, with the add-on itself in isputnik.home 4.74. An older home keeps working; the engine only stops answering on addresses nothing asks for any more.

label: Pictures for a film's parts
changes: **A film in several parts shows pictures for each part**: a part matched to an episode of a TV show on TMDB gets that episode's picture, name and description.
